title: Completed coefficient comparison and exceptional-adjoint model transport
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For a finite extension $B/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure write $R_B=\mathcal O_B$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $\mathcal D_B(W)=D^b_c(W,R_B)$ for the derived-complete integral constructible category over the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_{B,W}$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Put $P_B=Rf_{!,R_B}:\mathcal D_B(X)\to\mathcal D_B(Y)$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and $J_B=H_{f,R_B}$ with its tower adjunction $P_B\dashv J_B$, unit $\eta_B^J$, and counit $\epsilon_B^J$ [det-sp-integral-adjunction-bijection]. Composition below is right to left.

Let $E\subset F$ be such coefficient fields. For $W=X,Y$ let $T_{F/E}^W(-)=-\otimes^L_{\widehat R_{E,W}}\widehat R_{F,W}$, and let $C_{F/E}^W$ be the strict-tower completed integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Use the canonical natural completion isomorphism $\chi_{F/E}^W:T_{F/E}^W\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{F/E}^W$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Let $b^t:T^YP_E\xrightarrow{\sim}P_FT^X$ and $c^t:T^XJ_E\xrightarrow{\sim}J_FT^Y$ be the derived limits of the actual maps of coefficient towers in clauses (1)-(2) of [det-sp-field-extension-towers]. Then the formulas
$$b^0_M=P_F(\chi^X_M)b^t_M(\chi^Y_{P_EM})^{-1},\qquad c^0_K=J_F(\chi^Y_K)c^t_K(\chi^X_{J_EK})^{-1}$$
define natural isomorphisms for completed extension, with the identities
$$J_F(b^0_M)c^0_{P_EM}C^X(\eta_E^J(M))=\eta_F^J(C^XM),$$
$$\epsilon_F^J(C^YK)P_F(c^0_K)b^0_{J_EK}=C^Y(\epsilon_E^J(K)).$$

More generally, for each coefficient field $B$, let $G_B$ be any specified right adjoint to this same $P_B$ on the stated constructible categories, with unit $\eta_B^G$ and counit $\epsilon_B^G$. Let $\theta_B:J_B\xrightarrow{\sim}G_B$ be the unique counit-preserving isomorphism [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. Then
$$\epsilon_B^G P_B(\theta_B)=\epsilon_B^J,\qquad \theta_{B,P_BM}\eta_B^J(M)=\eta_B^G(M).$$
If a tensor-version right-adjoint comparison $\widetilde c^t:T^XG_E\to G_FT^Y$ is supplied and, with $b^t$, satisfies the two unit/counit identities above with $T,G$ in place of $C,J$, put
$$\widetilde c^0_K=G_F(\chi^Y_K)\widetilde c^t_K(\chi^X_{G_EK})^{-1},\qquad c^{0,J}_K=\theta_{F,C^YK}^{-1}\widetilde c^0_K C^X(\theta_{E,K}).$$
The pair $b^0,c^{0,J}$ satisfies exactly the displayed completed-extension unit and counit identities for $J$. In particular this applies to the constructible exceptional adjoint of [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint]. If $G=J$ and $\widetilde c^t=c^t$, this construction gives $c^{0,J}=c^0$.

For $E\subset F\subset L$, write $\alpha^{t,W}:T_{L/F}^WT_{F/E}^W\to T_{L/E}^W$ for tensor associativity. The natural isomorphism
$$\alpha^{C,W}=\chi_{L/E}^W\alpha^{t,W}T_{L/F}^W((\chi_{F/E}^W)^{-1})(\chi_{L/F,C_{F/E}^W(-)}^W)^{-1}$$
is the completed-extension associator whose rationalization is the canonical one in [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. The comparisons $b^0,c^0$ satisfy
$$P_L(\alpha^{C,X}_M)b^0_{L/F,C_{F/E}^XM}C_{L/F}^Y(b^0_{F/E,M})=b^0_{L/E,M}\alpha^{C,Y}_{P_EM},$$
$$J_L(\alpha^{C,Y}_K)c^0_{L/F,C_{F/E}^YK}C_{L/F}^X(c^0_{F/E,K})=c^0_{L/E,K}\alpha^{C,X}_{J_EK}.$$
For alternative $G$ models, if the supplied tensor comparisons obey the corresponding $G$ cocycle, the transported $c^{0,J}$ obeys this same $J$ cocycle. Identity extensions have the identity comparisons under the canonical coefficient unitors. All assertions concern the specified maps of towers and their limits, not an inference of equality from equality of finite reductions.

proof.text: Write $x=\chi^X$, $y=\chi^Y$ and omit $F/E$. The derived-completeness hypothesis needed for $x,y$ is part of $\mathcal D_E(W)$. The finite-free completed-scalar comparison supplies natural isomorphisms $x:T^X\cong C^X$, $y:T^Y\cong C^Y$ on these objects. The integral-adjunction theorem gives $P^{\mathrm{tow}}_B\dashv J_B$ for $P^{\mathrm{tow}}_B=R\bar f_*j_!$ of the integral direct-image tower theorem, and the tower theorem's $b^t,c^t$ are stated for this $P^{\mathrm{tow}}_B$. Clause (2) of the direct-image tower theorem gives a canonical isomorphism of $P^{\mathrm{tow}}_BM$ with the derived limit of $Rf_{!,n}$ of the reductions modulo $\ell^n$, with the same compactification; as $(\ell^n)=(\varpi_B^{en})$, this tower is the subsequence $n\mapsto en$ of the $\varpi_B$-power tower defining $P_B$, and restriction to it is a natural quasi-isomorphism of the product-cone limits by the Roos cofinality lemma (applied to the underlying abelian sheaves; the maps $a_e,b_e$ are $\widehat R_B$-linear). This gives $\omega_B:P^{\mathrm{tow}}_B\cong P_B$. Transport along $\omega$: $\eta^J=J(\omega)\eta^{\mathrm{tow}}$, $\epsilon^J=\epsilon^{\mathrm{tow}}\omega^{-1}_{J(-)}$, $b^t\mapsto\omega_{F,T^X}b^tT^Y(\omega_E^{-1})$; naturality of $c^t$ across $\omega_E$ shows the transported data satisfy the same unit, counit and cocycle equations. Clause (2) of the tower theorem supplies the actual $b^t,c^t$, their unit/counit equations and their tensor-associativity cocycles for chains $E\subset F\subset L$ (equalities allowed); identity normalization is not stated there and is derived in step 9. Thus the displayed composites defining $b^0,c^0$ are well typed and natural isomorphisms: $C^YP_E\to T^YP_E\to P_FT^X\to P_FC^X$ and $C^XJ_E\to T^XJ_E\to J_FT^Y\to J_FC^Y$.

proof.text:
For the unit substitute $b^0,c^0$. The adjacent $J_F(y_{P_EM}^{-1})J_F(y_{P_EM})$ cancel. Naturality of $x$ gives $x_{J_EP_EM}^{-1}C^X(\eta_E^J)=T^X(\eta_E^J)x_M^{-1}$. The left side of the required identity becomes
$$J_FP_F(x_M)J_F(b^t_M)c^t_{P_EM}T^X(\eta_E^J(M))x_M^{-1}=J_FP_F(x_M)\eta_F^J(T^XM)x_M^{-1}=\eta_F^J(C^XM).$$
The first equality is the tensor unit equation supplied by the tower theorem; the second is naturality of $\eta_F^J$.

proof.text:
For the counit, substitution cancels $P_F(x_{J_EK}^{-1})P_F(x_{J_EK})$. Naturality of $\epsilon_F^J$ then gives
$$\epsilon_F^J(C^YK)P_F(c^0_K)b^0_{J_EK}=y_K\epsilon_F^J(T^YK)P_F(c^t_K)b^t_{J_EK}y_{P_EJ_EK}^{-1}.$$
Apply the tensor counit equation of the tower theorem to obtain $y_KT^Y(\epsilon_E^J(K))y_{P_EJ_EK}^{-1}=C^Y(\epsilon_E^J(K))$, the last equality being naturality of $y$. These calculations apply unchanged to any supplied $\widetilde c^t$ with $G$ replacing $J$, since only its assumed equations and naturality were used. No invertibility of $\widetilde c^t$ is needed.

proof.text: Apply uniqueness of right adjoints to $P_B\dashv J_B$ and $P_B\dashv G_B$. It gives the natural isomorphism $\theta_B:J_B\cong G_B$ with $\epsilon_B^G P_B(\theta_B)=\epsilon_B^J$. To check its unit identity, transpose $\theta_{B,P_BM}\eta_B^J(M)$ under $P_B\dashv G_B$: its transpose is $\epsilon_B^G(P_BM)P_B(\theta_{B,P_BM})P_B(\eta_B^J(M))=\epsilon_B^J(P_BM)P_B(\eta_B^J(M))=1_{P_BM}$. This is also the transpose of $\eta_B^G(M)$, proving equality by the adjunction bijection. If $G_B=J_B$ with the same adjunction, uniqueness gives $\theta_B=1$.

proof.text:
For alternative models the calculations of steps 2--3 give the completed $G$ equations. Naturality of $\theta_F$ across $b^0_M$ and step 4 give
$$J_F(b^0_M)c^{0,J}_{P_EM}C^X(\eta_E^J)=\theta_{F,P_FC^XM}^{-1}G_F(b^0_M)\widetilde c^0_{P_EM}C^X(\eta_E^G)=\theta_{F,P_FC^XM}^{-1}\eta_F^G(C^XM)=\eta_F^J(C^XM).$$
For the counit use $\epsilon_F^JP_F(\theta_F^{-1})=\epsilon_F^G$ and naturality of $b^0$ across $\theta_{E,K}$:
$$\epsilon_F^JP_F(c^{0,J}_K)b^0_{J_EK}=\epsilon_F^GP_F(\widetilde c^0_K)b^0_{G_EK}C^Y(P_E\theta_{E,K})=C^Y(\epsilon_E^G P_E\theta_{E,K})=C^Y(\epsilon_E^J).$$
The integral exceptional-adjoint theorem provides the specified constructible right adjoint to this same $P_B$, so it is an allowed $G_B$. If $G=J$ with the same adjunction, step 4 gives $\theta=1$, and $\widetilde c^t=c^t$ gives the claimed equality $c^{0,J}=c^0$.

proof.text: Put $1=F/E$, $2=L/F$, $3=L/E$, and $z^W_K=\chi^W_{2,C^W_1K}T^W_2(\chi^W_{1,K})$. Naturality of $\chi_2$ also writes $z^W_K=C^W_2(\chi^W_{1,K})\chi^W_{2,T^W_1K}$. Thus the displayed $\alpha^{C,W}$ is $\chi^W_3\alpha^{t,W}(z^W)^{-1}$. The scalar-completion associator lemma states $a^C z=\chi_3\alpha^t$ for the actual quotient-cocone maps and the canonical completed associator. Cancel the isomorphism $z$ to identify $\alpha^C=a^C$. It also supplies the canonical unit normalization. The canonical isomorphism of the scalar-extension composition theorem is, in its bound statement (sfRationalScalarComp, unique by sfRationalScalarComp\_existsUnique), the componentwise localization of the ordinary balanced associator conjugated by the quotient-completion comparisons, which is $\chi_3\alpha^tz^{-1}=\alpha^C$; this is how the item's statement pins it; rational scalar extension is defined on integral representatives by precisely this completed functor. All its hypotheses are finite coefficient extensions and derived completeness; no flatness condition on an input complex is being added.

proof.text:
Here is the coefficient-cocycle calculation for $b$; write $b_i^0=P(\chi_i^X)b_i^t(\chi_i^Y P)^{-1}$ with the appropriate field subscripts on $P$. Let
$$D=P_L(\alpha^{C,X})b^0_{2,C^X_1(-)}C^Y_2(b^0_1).$$
Expand both $b^0$ factors and precompose $D$ with $z^Y_{P_E(-)}$. Naturality of $\chi_2^Y$ moves it across $b_1^0$, cancelling $(\chi_2^Y P_F)^{-1}\chi_2^Y P_F$; naturality of $b_2^t$ across $\chi_1^X$ then gives
$$D z^Y_{P_E(-)}=P_L(\alpha^{C,X}z^X)b^t_{2,T^X_1(-)}T^Y_2(b^t_1)
=P_L(\chi^X_3\alpha^{t,X})b^t_{2,T^X_1(-)}T^Y_2(b^t_1).$$
The tensor cocycle from the tower theorem turns this into $P_L(\chi^X_3)b^t_3\alpha^{t,Y}_{P_E(-)}$. Since $b^0_3\chi^Y_{3,P_E(-)}=P_L(\chi^X_3)b^t_3$ and $\alpha^{C,Y}z^Y=\chi^Y_3\alpha^{t,Y}$, this equals $b^0_3\alpha^{C,Y}_{P_E(-)}z^Y_{P_E(-)}$. Cancel $z^Y$ to obtain precisely the asserted $b^0$ cocycle.

proof.text:
For $c$ let $D'=J_L(\alpha^{C,Y})c^0_{2,C^Y_1(-)}C^X_2(c^0_1)$. Substitution and naturality, now moving $\chi_2^X$ across $c^0_1$ and $c^t_2$ across $\chi_1^Y$, give
$$D'z^X_{J_E(-)}=J_L(\alpha^{C,Y}z^Y)c^t_{2,T^Y_1(-)}T^X_2(c^t_1)
=J_L(\chi^Y_3\alpha^{t,Y})c^t_{2,T^Y_1(-)}T^X_2(c^t_1)
=J_L(\chi^Y_3)c^t_3\alpha^{t,X}_{J_E(-)}
=c^0_3\alpha^{C,X}_{J_E(-)}z^X_{J_E(-)}.$$
The middle equality is the tensor $c$ cocycle of the tower theorem; cancel $z^X$. The same expansion proves the completed $G$ cocycle from a supplied tensor $G$ cocycle, without requiring its comparisons invertible. Conjugation by $\theta$ then gives the $J$ cocycle: in the product of two transported comparisons the middle $C_2^X(\theta_F)C_2^X(\theta_F^{-1})$ cancels, and naturality of $\theta_L$ across $\alpha^{C,Y}$ and of $\alpha^{C,X}$ across $\theta_E$ leaves $\theta_L^{-1}$ times the $G$ cocycle times $C_2^XC_1^X(\theta_E)$. All equalities occur between the actual limit morphisms throughout.

proof.text: For identity extensions let $u^{t,W}:T^W_{B/B}\cong1$ be multiplication and $u^{C,W}=u^{t,W}(\chi^W_{B/B})^{-1}$; by the unit equations of the scalar-completion associator lemma and the case $L=E$ of the completion comparison this is the canonical completed unitor. The tower theorem does not state identity normalization; derive it from its cocycle for $B=B=B$, where for ordinary tensor $\alpha^t_{B/B/B}=u^t_{T(-)}$. Put $\beta_N=P_B(u^{t,X}_N)b^t_Nu^{t,Y\,-1}_{P_BN}:P_BN\to P_BN$. The cocycle $P_B(u^t_{TM})b^t_{TM}T^Y(b^t_M)=b^t_Mu^t_{TP_BM}$ and naturality $u^t_{P_BTM}T^Y(b^t_M)=b^t_Mu^t_{TP_BM}$ give $\beta_{TM}b^t_M=b^t_M$, so $\beta_{TM}=1$ as $b^t$ is invertible; naturality of $\beta$ across the isomorphism $u^t_M:TM\to M$ gives $\beta_M=1$, i.e. $P_B(u^{t,X})b^t=u^{t,Y}P_B$. The same computation with the $c$ cocycle and invertible $c^t$ gives $J_B(u^{t,Y})c^t=u^{t,X}J_B$. Substitute $b^0,c^0$ and cancel $\chi^{-1}\chi$: $P_B(u^{C,X})b^0=u^{C,Y}P_B$ and $J_B(u^{C,Y})c^0=u^{C,X}J_B$. For a supplied alternative $G$ comparison, not assumed invertible, its counit identity under these unitors with $b^0=1$ says $\epsilon_B^GP_B(\widetilde c)=\epsilon_B^G$; both $\widetilde c$ and $1_{G_B}$ have this transpose under $P_B\dashv G_B$, so $\widetilde c=1$ and the transported comparison is $\theta_B^{-1}\theta_B=1$. This includes repeated fields in coefficient towers.
